description: One SessionStart command hook (`agent-exec hook session-start`) injects the routing protocol, or the worker notice in a hosted worker's tree, at startup, resume, clear and compact; at every start it also appends orchestra's session env block (first line `# orchestra session env`) once to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, which Claude Code runs in front of every Bash command of the session, subagents' included: the Node CPU cap (NODE_OPTIONS, from throttle.test_slots) and, in a linked worktree, the pnpm global virtual store entries `agent-exec hook tree-env` prints for an orchestra tree, ending with the line `true`; it is a command hook, so it runs where cc-plugin-sec-default holds every classic.* mod event, and it is the only hook that re-injects after a compaction. It stamps the session so `agent-exec doctor` reports a skipped hook, and it fails open (a missing or unbuildable agent-exec is reported by doctor, not shown at every session start). The hooks module (orchestra.ts) listens only to events Claude Code does not hold from user-tier mods (tool.call, turn.start/turn.complete, prompt.submit, session.end, plus the HUD's and the board's own), so it works where cc-plugin-sec-default is seated, and it stamps the session too. It denies starting long-running work from any shell (agent-exec wave run outside the orchestra-wave agent's --detach, claude -p/--print, agent-exec dispatch without --detach; ORCHESTRA_LAUNCH_GUARD); asks the main thread to re-route once a turn hand-edits enforcement.turn_edits distinct files, the nudge riding on the edit's tool result; allows one orchestra-delegate per user prompt and denies the other orchestration agents until the user opts in or answers the one ask (enforcement.opt_in); denies merging, rebasing, resetting, pushing or branching from an orchestra/* branch outside an orchestra worktree, and merge commits of Agent worktree-* branches, loops and variable operands included, and points to `agent-exec isolate land` (enforcement.orchestra_merge); guards worker subagents against destructive VCS and the shared git stash (enforcement.worker_vcs), against writing the main working tree while they own a worktree (enforcement.worker_tree), against a second writer in a leased worktree (enforcement.worktree_lease), and against running the whole test suite (ORCHESTRA_TEST_GUARD), and against replacing NODE_OPTIONS or starting a test runner from node -e (the worker Node guard; `[orchestra:allow-node: <reason>]`, no switch); denies Agent, Task and Workflow calls while the plan's five-hour usage window is at or above enforcement.usage_guard (ORCHESTRA_USAGE_GUARD; orchestra-wave and orchestra-relay are exempt, and `[orchestra:allow-usage: <reason>]` in a main-thread Agent call lifts it twice per session); caps an orchestra-planner to orchestra-scout and orchestra-checker children, their count, concurrency and tool calls (enforcement.fanout, ORCHESTRA_FANOUT_GUARD; no per-call escape); denies SendMessage to an agent whose context reached enforcement.resume_max_tokens (ORCHESTRA_RESUME_GUARD; `[orchestra:allow-resume: <reason>]` once per agent, otherwise spawn a fresh agent with a handoff); the module runs its own plugin's bin/agent-exec, never the one on PATH; releases the lease on each subagent turn's end, where every orchestra:* subagent also leaves a handoff file (~/.local/state/claude-orchestra/handoffs/<session>/<agent>.md, kept 7 days: its goal, its answer, the commands that failed and the files to read) that the resume guard's deny names, and removes the session's clean orchestra worktrees at session.end (enforcement.session_cleanup); admits worker heavy commands machine-wide (throttle.heavy_slots, tests on throttle.test_slots); starts, on each main-loop turn, one detached process-guard watcher per Claude Code process (`agent-exec proc watch`), which kills the process tree under any child of that process (a Bash tool shell, a background command, an MCP server) that outgrows 200 processes or a quarter of memory, and says so on that call's tool result (the process guard; no switch); holds the orchestra-wave watcher to `agent-exec wave run … --detach` and `agent-exec wave wait --state <state> --max-wait <1-170> [--since <seq>]` in the foreground, denying every other command, a longer hop and run_in_background, and tells it on the tool result when a call was moved to the background or a wait answered running (the wave watcher guard; no switch); nudges once per session against generalist subagents that inherit the session model or name Fable (enforcement.opus_generalist) and, opt-in, direct Haiku spawns (enforcement.light_class); and shows running orchestra agents and the waves the orchestra-wave watcher (or an allowed main-thread launch) starts in one band above the prompt (terminal and desktop: a summary row naming each run's account, whose 詳細 button expands it to the running packages, needs and next; collapsed by default) and a detail pane (only when asked: /orchestra:progress toggles it, its own button closes it), toasting each new wave need (userConfig hud); and, once /orchestra:board has published this account's claude.ai page, mirrors ~/.local/state/claude-orchestra/status.json into it with ArtifactData under the session's own sign-in (no model; one document per machine, at most once a minute unless the summary changed, one writer per change; only where ArtifactData is allowed without asking, never in hosted workers or -p runs). The module never changes a tool call's input: it allows, denies, or adds context to the result, so auto mode's review of a call stands. Every guard but the process guard and the wave watcher guard has a switch or an escape hatch, and every guard fails open
